platform_notes: All Clover devices run Clover's own Android-based software and are managed from the Clover web dashboard (clover.com). Day-to-day work is done in Clover apps on the device (Register, Sale, Transactions, Tips, Closeout, Setup, Employees, Cash log, Reporting) or in the dashboard (Sales activity, Reports, Settings, New Sale / Virtual Terminal); Clover Go is a phone app. The help articles tell merchants to 'contact Clover support'; for our merchants that means our own support, so entries carry an escalate_to value instead.

entries.title: Turn offline payments on or off on a device
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Tap Offline payments.
For each device, choose 'Do not allow offline payments' or 'Allow offline payments on demand'.
Tap Save, then tap Allow.
entries.quote: Allow offline payments on demand.

entries.title: Set limits for offline payments
steps: Open the Setup app, tap Payments, then tap Offline payments.
Tap Edit next to a limit.
Set the limit for a single offline payment.
Set the total limit for all offline payments on this device.
Set the amount above which an offline payment needs merchant approval. To switch approval off, set it to the same amount as the single-payment limit.
Tap Save, then tap Allow.
entries.quote: Limit total offline payments to $__. This sets the total not-to-exceed amount for offline payments on this Clover device.

entries.title: What happens to payments taken while the device is offline
steps: With offline payments enabled, a device can keep taking payments without internet for up to 7 days.
When a connection comes back, the device submits the offline payments for authorization by itself.
Once they are authorized, deposits are made and customers get their receipts.
You need to be back online and logged in for the payments to process.
entries.quote: When a connection becomes available, your device automatically submits offline payments for authorization, and once authorized, you receive your deposits, and your customers receive receipts.

entries.title: An offline payment was declined after the device came back online
steps: An offline payment is not approved until the device is back online.
The merchant accepts the risk that it is declined or only partly paid at that point.
Examples given: the card is expired or canceled, or the PIN was incorrect.
entries.quote: When you take an offline payment, you accept the risk of a declined or partial payment when the device is back online.

entries.title: EBT and gift cards cannot be taken offline
steps: Offline payments do not work with EBT cards or gift cards.
Take those cards only when the device is online.
entries.quote: This feature is not available with Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) or gift cards.

entries.title: Do not uninstall the app while offline payments are waiting
steps: Do not uninstall the app while the device is offline.
Uninstalling deletes all payments taken while offline.
entries.quote: Do not uninstall the app while offline. Doing so deletes all payments taken while offline.

entries.title: Offline payment declined or asks for approval because of the offline limit
steps: Offline payments above the single-payment limit are declined or need the merchant's approval.
Once the total of all offline payments reaches the total limit, the device stops taking offline payments.
To change the limits, open the Setup app, tap Payments, then Offline payments, and tap Edit next to the limit.
entries.quote: offline payments of $50 or higher are declined or require the merchant's approval

entries.title: Set offline payment options from the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Transactions, select Payments.
Scroll down to Offline Payments and select Edit.
For each device, choose whether to allow offline payments and set any limits.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Scroll down to the page until you find Offline Payments.

entries.title: Which devices have offline payments on by default
steps: Offline payments are set per device.
The article lists the option as enabled by default for Clover Station, Station 2, Clover Mini, Flex and Mobile.
If the device is set to 'Do not allow offline payments', it declines all offline transactions.
entries.quote: Do not allow offline payments: The Clover device declines all offline transactions.

entries.title: Log in to the Clover dashboard
steps: In a browser, go to clover.com and select Log in, or go to clover.com/login.
Select Access your account.
Enter the email address tied to your Clover account. For an owner this is the email used to sign up; for an employee it is the email the manager or owner entered for them.
Check your email for a message with a link to set a password and log in.
entries.quote: Check your email — you'll receive a message with a unique link to set a password and log in.

entries.title: No login email arrives after entering your email address
steps: If the email does not arrive right away, the address entered does not match the one in the Clover system.
Try again and make sure the email is typed correctly.
entries.quote: If you don’t receive an email right away, the email you entered doesn’t match the email in the Clover system.

entries.title: Forgot the dashboard password, or never set one
steps: Go to clover.com/login.
Select Access your account.
Enter the email address tied to your Clover account.
Use the link in the email you receive to set a password and log in.
entries.quote: If you don’t remember your password or did not set one, follow the steps to log in to your Clover account.

entries.title: Find your merchant ID (MID)
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under About your business, select Business information.
The MID is shown next to the business name.
entries.quote: Your MID is displayed next to your business name.

entries.title: Merchant ID versus Clover ID
steps: The merchant ID (MID) identifies the merchant account. It is typically 10 digits but can be 7 to 15.
The Clover ID is different: a 13-character code of letters and numbers that identifies the Clover software.
entries.quote: Clover merchant ID numbers are typically 10 digits long, but they may range from 7 to 15 digits.

entries.title: Where the Help option is on Clover
steps: On the dashboard, select Help at the top.
On a Clover device, tap Help on the home screen.
In the Clover Go app, open the menu and tap Help.
A direct support phone number is printed on the statement.
entries.quote: On a Clover device, tap Help on the home screen.

entries.title: Add or adjust a tip in the Transactions app
steps: On the device, open the Transactions app.
Select the transaction.
Tap Add tip to add a tip from the paper receipt, or tap Edit to adjust a tip.
Enter the tip amount.
Tap Done.
If the device asks, tap Confirm tip.
entries.quote: To add a tip from the paper receipt, tap Add tip.

entries.title: Add or adjust tips in the Tips app
steps: On the device, open the Tips app.
Select the transaction.
Enter the tip amount from the paper receipt, or enter the correct amount to adjust it.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: On your Clover device, open the Tips app.

entries.title: Cannot add or adjust a tip
steps: Check whether the tip was entered on the device screen at checkout. Those tips cannot be added to or adjusted.
Check whether the transaction has already been batched or closed out. Tips cannot be added after that.
Check that the employee has permission to adjust tips (access to the Transactions app or Tips app).
Check that the tip entry location is set to 'On paper receipt'.
If tips still cannot be adjusted, contact support and ask for tip adjustment to be enabled.
entries.quote: The transaction has already been batched or closed.
entries.note: Last step needs support: tip adjustment is enabled on the account.

entries.title: Tip entry on paper receipt cannot be set, or tip adjustment is not available
steps: Contact support (the article says Clover support).
Ask for tip adjustment to be enabled.
entries.quote: Note: If you are unable to adjust tips, contact Clover support and request that the tip adjustment be enabled.

entries.title: Device asks to 'Confirm tip'
steps: The device shows this when the tip entered is unusually high or low.
Check the amount, then tap Confirm tip if it is right.
entries.quote: If you've entered an unusually high or low tip, your device will prompt you to tap Confirm tip to confirm the tip amount.

entries.title: Turn on dynamic tipping on a device
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Tips.
Select Dynamic tip configuration.
Select the 'Enable dynamic tipping methods' checkbox.
Tap Save.
Choose how customers enter tips: on-screen, on paper receipt, or no tip.
entries.quote: Select the Enable dynamic tipping methods checkbox.

entries.title: Turn on dynamic tipping from the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Tips.
Select Dynamic tip configuration.
Turn on 'Enable dynamic tipping methods'.
Save.
entries.quote: Turn on Enable dynamic tipping methods.

entries.title: Transactions app or Tips app for entering tips
steps: Both apps can add or adjust tips.
Use the Transactions app to work on one specific transaction.
Use the Tips app to enter many paper-receipt tips, typically after a shift.
entries.quote: Use the Tips app when your primary goal is to enter or manage tips.

entries.title: Choose where customers enter a tip (screen or printed receipt)
steps: Open the Setup app.
Select Tips > Tip entry location.
Select 'On tablet screen' or 'On printed receipt'.
From the dropdown, choose all devices or a single device.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Select On tablet screen or On printed receipt.

entries.title: No tip prompt on a cash payment
steps: This is expected. When a customer pays with cash, the device does not ask for a tip.
entries.quote: If a customer pays with cash, the Clover device does not request a tip.

entries.title: Turn tips on or off
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Tips.
Enable or disable tips and select Save.
Once enabled, tipping is active on the device.
entries.quote: Enable or disable tips and select Save. Once enabled, tipping will be active on your Clover device.

entries.title: Account is not set up to take tips
steps: Tip acceptance is configured by business type; tips are disabled automatically for retail businesses.
If the account is not set up to take tips, contact support.
entries.quote: If your account isn't set up to take tips, you can contact Clover support.

entries.title: What closeout (closing the batch) is
steps: Each day, card transactions are bundled into an open batch.
The batch stays open so adjustments such as paper-receipt tips can be made.
At closeout the batch closes and the card transactions are sent for clearing and settlement, then deposited.
Deposits are typically funded within 1-3 business days after the batch closes.
entries.quote: Each day, all of your Clover credit and debit card transactions are bundled together into an open batch.

entries.title: Change the closeout method (auto or manual)
steps: Contact support (the article says Clover support).
The closeout method cannot be changed by the merchant.
entries.quote: Contact Clover support to change your closeout method.

entries.title: Auto-closeout versus manual closeout
steps: Auto-closeout: the system collects each day's card sales and submits them automatically during a 50-minute window.
Manual closeout (US only): you must close the batch yourself each day, which lets you enter and adjust tips at your convenience.
entries.quote: Manual closeout (available in the US only): With manual closeout, you must manually close your batch each day.

entries.title: How auto-closeout works
steps: The system submits the day's card sales automatically during a 50-minute window.
The window is generally scheduled after the end of the business day; its start is the closeout time.
Tips entered on the device are included automatically.
entries.quote: Tips added directly from a Clover device are automatically accounted for with auto-closeout and do not need to be manually adjusted.

entries.title: Paper-receipt tips when the batch closes automatically
steps: Enter paper-receipt tips at least 50 minutes before the closeout time.
This gives the system time to process the adjustments before the batch is submitted.
entries.quote: you need to add them manually 50 minutes prior to your closeout time

entries.title: Batch closed automatically before paper tips were entered
steps: Tips not entered before the auto-closeout are lost.
Contact support (the article says Clover support). They can help add unentered tips after a closeout.
This is a manual process and delays the funding of that batch.
entries.quote: Contact Clover support for help adding unentered tips after a closeout event; however, this is a manual process that will delay your batch’s funding schedule.

entries.title: Device was offline at the auto-closeout time
steps: If the device is offline, the auto-closeout may not complete as expected.
Make sure the device is connected to the internet at the scheduled closeout time.
entries.quote: If your device is offline, the auto-closeout may not complete as expected.

entries.title: Closing the batch by hand when auto-closeout is on
steps: You can close the batch manually even when the system is set to auto-closeout.
Auto-closeout still runs at the scheduled closeout time.
entries.quote: You can manually close your batch if your system is set for auto-closeout. Auto-closeout will still occur at your scheduled closeout time.

entries.title: No Edit link next to the closeout time
steps: Only some account owners and admins can change the closeout time on the dashboard.
If the Edit link is not there, contact support to change the time.
entries.quote: If the Edit link is not available next to the closeout time, contact Clover support to change it.

entries.title: Change the auto-closeout time
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under About your business, select Closeout settings.
Select Edit next to Closeout time.
Check the hours of operation and select Confirm (or Edit them first).
On the 'Choose closeout time' page, select an auto-closeout window.
Select Continue, review, and select Confirm.
entries.quote: Select Edit next to Closeout time.

entries.title: How often the closeout time can be changed
steps: The closeout time can be changed only once in 7 days.
Allow up to 12 hours for the new time to take effect.
The user needs the Access Closeout permission.
entries.quote: You can change the closeout time only once in 7 days. Allow up to 12 hours for the new closeout time to take effect.

entries.title: Switch from manual closeout to auto-closeout
steps: Contact support (the article says Clover support).
Ask for the closeout method to be changed to auto-closeout.
entries.quote: If you are using manual closeout, contact Clover support to change the closeout method to auto-closeout.

entries.title: How long auto-closeout takes
steps: It can take up to 50 minutes for the system to close and submit the batch.
If possible, complete all transactions before the closeout time.
Deposits are settled in 1-3 days.
entries.quote: It can take up to 50 minutes for the system to close and submit your batch for processing.

entries.title: Check batch totals during the day
steps: On the device, open the Closeout app.
Review the totals for the batch, each card type, and each server.
Optionally print a report for each total.
entries.quote: Review the totals for batch, card type, and server.

entries.title: Transactions that are not included in the batch
steps: Open transactions are not in a batch until they are completed.
Transactions that are authorized but not yet approved are left out of the current batch and go into the next one.
Some transactions take longer to process, especially when the customer pays after the order is taken.
entries.quote: Any authorized but not yet approved transactions are excluded from the current batch but will be included in the next one.

entries.title: Stop the batch report printing automatically after closeout (device)
steps: Open the Closeout app.
Open the menu and tap Settings.
Clear the 'Auto Print Closeout Report' or 'Print Batch Report Automatically' checkbox.
Exit the settings screen to apply the change.
entries.quote: Clear the Auto Print Closeout Report or Print Batch Report Automatically checkbox to stop automatic printing of the batch report after each closeout.

entries.title: Stop the batch report printing automatically after closeout (dashboard)
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under About your business, select Closeout settings.
Turn off the toggle for automatic printing of the batch report.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Turn off the toggle icon to stop automatic printing of the batch report after each closeout.

entries.title: Closeout settings on the device (offline transactions, email, print)
steps: Open the Closeout app.
Open the menu and select Settings.
Choose the options you want: allow offline transactions during closeout, email the closeout report automatically, print the closeout report automatically.
The device must be online for the email and reporting features, and the user needs the Closeout > View closeout settings permission.
entries.quote: Allow offline transactions during closeout.

entries.title: Forgot to close the batch manually
steps: There are limits on how long a batch can stay open and how long transactions can be adjusted.
If the batch is not closed within those limits, transactions in the open batch may be lost.
The time limit is given when the merchant starts using Clover; contact support with questions.
entries.quote: If you don’t close your batch within these timeframes, transactions in the open batch may be lost.

entries.title: Closing the batch more than once in a day
steps: You can close the batch several times a day for your records.
All batches closed on the same day are grouped into a single deposit.
You will see several closeout reports but one deposit, minus fees and adjustments.
entries.quote: You can close your batch multiple times for your records, but you’ll receive only one deposit per day.

entries.title: Closing the batch on one device closes all devices
steps: When the batch is closed manually on one device, orders on the other Clover devices are closed too.
Tips for those orders can no longer be entered or edited.
entries.quote: When you manually close a batch on one device, all orders on your other Clover devices are also closed, and you cannot enter or edit tips for those orders.

entries.title: Close out the batch manually
steps: Enter all tips from paper receipts first.
Close any open tabs.
On the device, tap Closeout.
Review the details for the current batch.
Optionally print reports.
Tap Close Out All Devices and confirm.
Optionally tap 'Notify me when closed' to hear a sound and get an email when it is done.
entries.quote: Tap Close Out All Devices and confirm.

entries.title: Closeout shows a message asking for tips
steps: If you close out manually without adding tips, a message asks you to enter them before continuing.
Enter the tips from paper receipts before closing; tips not entered before settlement are lost.
Tips entered in the Tips app are added at the time of closeout.
entries.quote: If you close out manually without adding tips, a message appears and prompts you to enter them before continuing.

entries.title: Manual closeout is only available on a Clover device
steps: You cannot close out manually from the dashboard.
Batches on the Clover Go app close automatically.
Closing the batch manually on any other device also closes the Clover Go batch.
entries.quote: Note: Manual closeout can only be accessed from Clover devices.

entries.title: Batch status shows OPEN or CLOSED
steps: Open batches show OPEN with an exclamation mark, even when the batch total is $0.
Closed batches show CLOSED with a check mark.
Closeout processing can take up to 50 minutes.
entries.quote: Open batches appear as OPEN with an exclamation mark, even when the batch totals $0. Closed batches appear as CLOSED with a check mark.

entries.title: View or print the closeout report on a device
steps: Open the Closeout app (the article names Station, Mini and Flex).
View the batch and closeout details.
Print reports to receipt paper, or switch on the option to email the closeout report to the owner after closing a batch.
The user needs the Access Closeout > Print closeout reports permission.
entries.quote: View and print reports to receipt paper or activate an option to automatically email the closeout report to the owner's email after closing a batch.

entries.title: View closeout details on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
On the left, select Finances.
entries.quote: On the left, select Finances to view your closeout details.

entries.title: Get the closeout report by email
steps: Only the account owner can receive the closeout report by email.
Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Notification Preferences.
Select Edit.
Tick the email checkbox for closeout notifications and save.
entries.quote: Only the account owner may receive the batch closeout report by email.

entries.title: Stop the totals report printing at automatic closeout
steps: Open the Closeout app.
Open the menu and tap Settings.
Clear the 'Auto-print Totals Report on closeout' checkbox.
Exit the settings screen.
entries.quote: Clear the 'Auto-print Totals Report on closeout' checkbox to stop automatic printing of the batch report after each closeout.

entries.title: When the deposit arrives after closeout
steps: The deposit is credited to the bank account within 1-3 business days.
It shows the batch total minus processing fees and any adjustments.
entries.quote: Your deposit will be credited to your bank account within 1-3 business days, and it will display the batch total, minus processing fees and any adjustments.
entries.note: Questions about a specific deposit are a money matter.

entries.title: Void a payment right after the sale
steps: On the customer receipt screen that appears after the payment is approved, tap Void.
Confirm the void.
entries.quote: On the customer receipt screen that appears after a payment is approved, tap Void.

entries.title: Void a payment from the Transactions app
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Tap the transaction.
Tap Void.
Confirm the void.
entries.quote: Tap the transaction you want to cancel.

entries.title: Void a payment on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Transactions.
Select the Payments tab.
Find and select the payment.
Select Void or Cancel Payment.
Confirm.
entries.quote: Select Void or Cancel Payment.

entries.title: Only Refund is offered, there is no Void button
steps: The 25-minute void window has passed, or the daily batch has already closed.
The payment has settled, so issue a refund instead.
entries.quote: If the Void button is missing, your 25-minute void window has passed or your system has already completed its daily batch close.

entries.title: How long a payment can be voided
steps: A payment can be voided within 25 minutes of the sale, before the batch closes.
After 25 minutes, or once the daily batch has closed, it must be refunded instead.
Tapping Refund within 25 minutes is processed as a void behind the scenes.
entries.quote: Note: If you tap Refund within 25 minutes of the sale, the system will process it as a void behind the scenes.

entries.title: Customer still sees a pending charge after a void
steps: A void stops the transaction before it settles, so the funds never leave the customer's account.
The pending charge can still show on their online banking for 1-3 business days, depending on their bank.
entries.quote: However, the pending charge may still appear on their online banking for 1–3 business days, depending on their bank.

entries.title: Employee cannot void a payment
steps: The employee's role needs the 'Void payments' permission.
entries.quote: Permissions: To void a payment, employees must have the Void payments permission enabled.

entries.title: Difference between Void and Cancel
steps: Void removes a completed payment before it settles in the daily batch.
Cancel stops a transaction that is still pending or in progress and was never completed.
entries.quote: A Cancel terminates a transaction that is currently pending or still in progress (mid-flow) and has not yet been successfully completed.

entries.title: Voiding a payment versus voiding a pre-auth
steps: Voiding a payment cancels a completed sale and must be done within 25 minutes.
Voiding a pre-auth removes a temporary card hold and can be done any time before the final amount is captured.
entries.quote: Voiding a pre-auth simply removes a temporary card hold (often used for bar tabs or incidentals), and can be done at any time before the final amount is captured.

entries.title: Internet dropped while a card was processing
steps: If a network connection error happens during a payment request, the Clover system voids the payment automatically.
This is so the customer is not charged for a failed transaction.
entries.quote: If a network connection error occurs during a payment request, the Clover system will automatically void the payment on the backend to ensure the customer is not accidentally charged for a failed transaction.

entries.title: Refund a payment (full or partial) in the Transactions app
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Find and tap the transaction.
Tap Refund.
Enter the amount: the maximum shown for a full refund, or a smaller amount for a partial refund.
Optionally choose whether to refund the tip.
Confirm the refund.
entries.quote: Select the transaction, and tap Refund.

entries.title: Refund specific items in the Orders app
steps: Open the Orders app (if the service plan includes it).
Find and tap the order.
Tap Refund.
Choose 'Refund items' and select the items, or 'Refund payment' and select the payment.
Review and confirm the refund.
entries.quote: Refund items: Select the item or items you want to refund.

entries.title: Refund a payment (full or partial) on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Transactions.
On the Payments tab, find the payment.
Select Details, then Refund.
Enter the amount, up to the maximum shown.
Optionally choose whether to refund the tip.
Select Refund and then Confirm refund.
Check it on the Refunds tab.
entries.quote: Select Refund $XX.XX and then Confirm refund to complete the refund.

entries.title: Which app to use for a refund
steps: It depends on the service plan.
The Transactions app refunds a full or partial amount.
The Orders app, if included, refunds specific items or exchanges an item.
entries.quote: If your service plan includes the Orders app, you can use it to refund specific items or exchange an item.

entries.title: How long after a sale a refund can be made
steps: Refunds go back to the original form of payment.
Typically refunds can be processed for up to 120 days after the transaction.
Some processing fees may apply; policies depend on the merchant agreement.
entries.quote: Typically, refunds can be processed for up to 120 days after the transaction.
entries.note: Fee and policy questions are a money matter.

entries.title: Cancel a refund that has not processed yet
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Transactions.
Find the refund and select Details.
If the option is available, tap Issue Void.
entries.quote: Find the refund you want to void, then select Details.

entries.title: Give an employee role permission to refund
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Under Employees, select Employee permissions.
Under Access Register, select View App Permissions, then the pencil icon next to Refund Payments.
Select the role and select the check mark to add it.
entries.quote: Under Access Register, select View App Permissions; then select the pencil icon next to Refund Payments.

entries.title: Refund button does not appear on the dashboard
steps: Two-factor authentication must be turned on for the Refund button to appear.
Turn on two-factor authentication for the account.
Also check the user has the Access transactions > Refund payments permission.
entries.quote: The Refund button appears in your transaction payments only when two-factor authentication is enabled.

entries.title: Refund a Virtual Terminal payment
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales Activity > Transactions. Virtual Terminal payments are labelled Virtual Terminal.
Find the transaction and select Details.
Select Issue Refund.
Enter the amount, up to the maximum shown.
Select Refund and then Confirm Refund.
entries.quote: Virtual Terminal transactions appear in Transactions with the label Virtual Terminal.

entries.title: Refund an online order on the device
steps: On a device only the full order can be refunded.
Open the Transactions app.
Tap the transaction.
Tap Refund and confirm.
Select where to apply the refund.
Tap Close window when the success message appears.
entries.quote: Select where to apply the refund. Once the refund is complete, a success message appears.

entries.title: Refund an online order (full or partial) on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales Activity > Transactions.
Find the payment and select Details.
Select the refund reason, then Next.
Enter the refund amount.
Select Confirm refund, then Got it.
entries.quote: Select the refund reason, and then select Next.

entries.title: Refunding an order from a third-party ordering partner
steps: Only orders from Clover Online Ordering and Order With Google can be refunded in Clover.
For all other third-party ordering partners, the third party must issue the refund to the customer.
entries.quote: For all other third-party ordering partners, refunds need to be issued by the third-party directly to the customer.

entries.title: A Klarna sale cannot be voided
steps: Klarna does not support voiding a completed sale on Clover devices.
Process a full or partial refund instead, from the device or the dashboard.
The refund must be tied to an existing Klarna transaction; manual or unmatched refunds are not possible.
Klarna does not support reversing a refund.
entries.quote: On Clover devices, Klarna does not support voiding completed sales.

entries.title: Klarna does not show as a payment option
steps: Klarna works only when the device is online; it is not available in offline mode.
If the business takes tips on paper, Klarna does not appear. Klarna supports tips on the device screen only.
Check the device is one the article lists: Flex 2, 3, 4 and Flex Pocket; Mini 2, 3; Compact; Kiosk; Station Duo 2; Station 2018 tethered to Mini.
entries.quote: If your business uses tips on paper, Klarna will not appear as a payment method.

entries.title: Void a pre-authorization on the device
steps: Open the Register app.
Select the order or transaction.
Tap More at the bottom left.
Select Void pre-auth.
Confirm.
entries.quote: Void a pre-authorization on the device

entries.title: Complete a pre-authorization as a sale on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Transactions.
Select the Authorizations tab.
Find the pre-authorization and select Complete transaction.
Enter the final amount.
Select Save or Complete.
entries.quote: Find the pre-authorization you want to capture and select Complete transaction.

entries.title: Completing a pre-auth for a higher amount is declined
steps: When the final amount is higher than the pre-auth, the system requests approval for the difference.
If that is declined, a notification appears.
Either capture the last approved amount, or cancel and enter a new amount.
entries.quote: If declined: A notification will prompt you to either proceed capturing the last approved authorized amount or cancel to enter a new amount.

entries.title: Pre-authorizations and closing the batch
steps: Closing the batch does not void a pre-authorization.
A pre-authorization stays in place until the customer pays or it is voided.
entries.quote: Closing out a batch does not void a pre-authorization.

entries.title: How much a pre-auth can be completed for
steps: The final amount can be less than, or up to 200% more than, the original authorization.
Clover recommends not going over 120% of the original amount, to reduce the risk of large chargebacks.
entries.quote: To reduce the risk of large chargebacks, Clover recommends that you do not exceed 120% of the original authorization amount.

entries.title: Customer asks when a voided pre-auth hold will drop off
steps: Voiding a pre-auth removes the hold but does not delete the order.
How long the hold takes to disappear varies by bank.
The customer should ask their bank.
entries.quote: The time it takes to remove the hold varies by bank. Customers should contact their bank with questions about a hold.

entries.title: Create a pre-authorization in Virtual Terminal
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select New Sale.
From Transaction Type, select Pre-authorization.
Enter the amount.
Enter the customer's payment information.
Select Pre-authorize Payment.
entries.quote: From Transaction Type, select Pre-authorization.

entries.title: Void an authorization on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales Activity > Transactions.
Select Authorizations.
Find the authorization.
Select Options > Void authorization.
Select Void on the confirmation message.
entries.quote: For the authorization, select Options > Void authorization.

entries.title: Multi-capture (several charges on one authorization) is not available
steps: Multi-capture has to be enabled on the account.
Contact support to enable it.
entries.quote: In order to enable multi-capture, please contact customer support.

entries.title: Start multi-capture on an authorization
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales Activity > Transactions > Authorizations.
On the authorization, select Options > Initiate multi-capture.
Enter the amount for the first transaction.
Select Charge.
entries.quote: Identify the authorization you want to work with and select Options > Initiate multi-capture.

entries.title: Take the next or final charge on a multi-capture authorization
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Transactions, then the Authorizations tab.
Select Manage multi-capture.
Enter the amount of the next transaction.
If it is the last one, tick 'This is the final transaction'; this voids the remaining authorization and closes it.
Select Charge.
entries.quote: Selecting that option will void the remaining authorization and close the authorization.

entries.title: Take a phone or mail order payment in the Phone Sale app
steps: Open the Phone Sale app.
Enter the amount and tap Phone Sale.
Optionally enter the customer's billing ZIP code and street address, then tap Continue.
If asked, enter the invoice or identification number and tap Continue.
Follow the prompts to complete the payment.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: Enter the amount of the sale, and tap Phone Sale.

entries.title: Take a phone or mail order payment in the Register app
steps: Open the Register app.
Enter the sale and tap Pay.
On the Pay Full Amount tab, under Other, select Mail/Phone Order.
Follow the prompts.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: In the Pay Full Amount tab, under Other, select Mail/Phone Order.

entries.title: Which app takes keyed phone or mail payments
steps: It depends on the service plan: either the Phone Sale app or the Register app.
These payments are processed as card-not-present transactions.
entries.quote: Depending on your service plan, you use either the Phone Sale app or the Register app on your Clover device to manually enter card details and process phone or mail payments.

entries.title: Register app or Sale app for a sale
steps: Use the Register app (where available) to add items; the system works out taxes and totals.
Use the Sale app to simply enter the full amount.
entries.quote: Use the Sale app to simply enter the full amount.

entries.title: Take a PayPal or Venmo payment by QR code
steps: Open the Register app or the Sale app.
Tap the items or enter the amount.
Tap Pay.
On a Station Duo tap Options > Scan QR code; on other devices tap QR code.
Have the customer add a tip on the device if applicable.
Ask the customer to scan the QR code with their phone and confirm the amount there.
entries.quote: On a Station Duo, tap Options > Scan QR code.

entries.title: PayPal and Venmo payments are missing from the Closeout app
steps: This is expected. The Closeout app shows only credit and debit transactions.
In the Reporting app, PayPal and Venmo show as separate tender types.
entries.quote: The Closeout app does not display individual transactions using the PayPal or Venmo payment method, as the app only shows credit and debit transactions.

entries.title: Take a payment when cash discount is on
steps: Open the Register app or Sale app.
Add items or an amount.
Select Pay. Both the regular price and the cash discount price appear.
If you select Cash, enter the cash received.
If you select Charge, the customer-facing screen shows both prices.
entries.quote: Select Pay. Both the total regular price and the cash discount price appear.

entries.title: Turn on cash discount on a device
steps: On a Station, Mini, Flex, Kiosk or Compact, open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Scroll down and tap Cash discount.
Tick the checkbox to enable it.
Enter the discount percentage.
Select Tenders and choose which payment methods get the cash-discounted price.
Tap Save and accept the Terms and Conditions.
entries.quote: On a Station, Mini, Flex, Kiosk, or Compact, open the Setup app.
entries.note: Cash discount ties to the processing agreement; rate and agreement questions are a money matter.

entries.title: Turn cash discount off
steps: Turning cash discount off may need support, especially if new agreements on processing rates were signed.
Contact support (the article says Clover support).
entries.quote: To turn off cash discount, you may need to contact Clover support, especially if any new agreements regarding processing rates were signed.

entries.title: Cash discount rate and how to change it
steps: The rate is 4% by default.
It can be set between 1% and 5%, in steps of 0.25%.
Change it in the account settings; if inventory prices were adjusted for the discount, re-adjust them for the new rate.
entries.quote: The cash discount rate is 4% by default, but you can adjust it between 1% to 5% and change it in increments of .25%.

entries.title: Cash discount, sales tax and tips
steps: Cash discount is applied before tax, automatically. Tax on taxable items is added after the discount.
It is applied before any tip, so the discount does not include the tip.
entries.quote: Before. Cash discount is applied pre-tax, automatically.

entries.title: Cash discount on split payments
steps: Each split is treated as its own transaction.
A split paid in cash gets the cash discount price.
entries.quote: Yes, each split is treated as an individual transaction, which can be paid in cash at the cash discount price.

entries.title: Set a maximum payment amount (payment threshold)
steps: On the device, open the Setup app.
Select Payments.
Select Payment Threshold.
Enter the threshold amount.
Decide whether to allow manager overrides.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select Payment Threshold.

entries.title: A payment is over the payment threshold
steps: If manager overrides are allowed: select Edit amount and enter a lower amount, or select Enter manager passcode and have a manager enter their passcode.
If manager overrides are not allowed: reduce the payment amount, and split the total into several payments if needed.
entries.quote: If you have not enabled manager overrides and the transaction exceeds the set payment threshold, the employee will be required to reduce the payment amount for the current transaction and, potentially, split the transaction amount into multiple payments.

entries.title: Make the device ask customers for a PIN
steps: On the device, open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Tap Prompt for PIN.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Whether or not to prompt customers for a PIN during transactions.

entries.title: Show letters on the PIN pad
steps: On the device, open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Tap PIN Entry.
Under 'Alphabetic characters on PIN pad', select Enable.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Under Alphabetic characters on PIN pad, select Enable.

entries.title: Accept purchasing cards as a tender type
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Tap Tenders accepted.
Select Purchasing Card, then tick Accept tender.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Select Purchasing Card; then check Accept tender.

entries.title: Purchasing card swiped on an FD40 PIN pad runs as a normal card
steps: The FD40 PIN pad does not support the purchasing card tender type.
A purchasing card swiped on it runs like a regular debit or credit card.
entries.quote: Note: The FD40 PIN pad doesn’t support the purchasing card tender type.

entries.title: Take a purchasing card payment on a device
steps: Swipe the purchasing card. The device recognizes it.
Optionally tap Continue to give more information about the card.
Optionally enter purchase information on the Purchasing Card Information screen.
Tap Continue to complete the payment.
If the extra information is skipped, the payment runs as a regular credit or debit card payment.
entries.quote: Swipe the purchasing card. Your Clover device recognizes the card as a purchasing card.

entries.title: Getting set up to use purchasing cards (Level 2 / Level 3 data)
steps: Purchasing cards need to be set up by the processor (the article says to contact Fiserv).
A tax ID number is required.
entries.quote: To use purchasing cards, please contact Fiserv. You will be required to provide your tax ID number.

entries.title: Choose which payment types (tenders) the device accepts
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Tap Tenders accepted.
Tick or clear 'Accept tender' for each type.
Optionally tick 'Opens cash drawer' for a type.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Accept tender: Select to allow customers to use the tender type for payments.

entries.title: Add a custom tender type (for example store credit)
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Payments, then Tenders Accepted.
Tap the plus button.
Enter a name and tick Accept tender.
Tap Save.
Do not create a custom tender for something Clover already supports, such as cash, credit, debit or EBT.
entries.quote: Note: Do not create a custom tender type for payment methods that Clover already supports, such as cash, credit, debit, or EBT cards.

entries.title: Custom tender payments are not funded
steps: A custom tender only tracks the payment separately.
No card or account number is entered and no funding is provided.
entries.quote: No cards or account numbers are entered for custom tenders, and no funding is provided.

entries.title: Cash drawer does not open for a payment type
steps: Open the Setup app, tap Payments, then Tenders accepted.
Check that 'Opens cash drawer' is ticked for that tender type. When it is cleared the drawer does not open.
Clover Flex and Mobile devices do not open the cash drawer automatically.
entries.quote: Note: Clover Flex and Mobile devices do not automatically open the cash drawer.

entries.title: Sell an age-restricted item
steps: Open the Register app or Clover Dining app.
Select the item.
When asked, confirm the customer's age. The item is added only after age confirmation.
Continue and complete the order.
entries.quote: If the item is age-restricted, confirm the customer’s age. The item is added to the order after age confirmation.

entries.title: Remove an item from an order before payment
steps: Open the Register app.
Tap the item you want to remove.
Tap Delete.
Deleting items and editing printed items without an override needs the Register permission.
entries.quote: Tap the item you want to remove.

entries.title: Reprint or resend a customer receipt
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Find the paid transaction.
Reissue the customer receipt from there.
entries.quote: You can use the Transactions app to locate paid transactions and reissue customer receipts.
entries.note: The public article gives no further steps; the detailed article needs a Clover login.

entries.title: Print a customer receipt automatically after each order
steps: Open the Setup app on a Station, Mini or Flex (Settings on a Compact).
Tap Payment receipts.
Tick 'Automatically print customer receipt after each order'.
entries.quote: Open the Setup app from the home screen of your Station, Mini, or Flex, or Settings on a Compact.

entries.title: Skip the receipt screen after a payment
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Payment receipts.
Tap Skip receipt screen.
entries.quote: (Optional) Tap Skip receipt screen, then begin the next transaction to bypass it.

entries.title: No Print button in the Register app
steps: The Print button appears in the Register app only when the 'Print order receipt manually in the Register' option is enabled.
entries.quote: The Print button only appears in the Register app when you enable the Print order receipt manually in the Register option.

entries.title: Hide the street address on receipts
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Payment receipts.
Tick the 'Hide street address' checkbox.
Select Save.
Receipts then show only city, state and zip code.
entries.quote: Once you turn on the setting, only the city, state, and zip code will appear on receipts.

entries.title: Change what prints on customer receipts
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Transactions, select Payment receipts.
Choose the options: header and footer text, logo, order note, cashier name, line items, barcode, customer information and others.
Select Save.
A logo can only be uploaded on the dashboard.
entries.quote: Logos and images can only be uploaded on the dashboard.

entries.title: Bottom of the Clover Mini receipt is lost when tearing it off
steps: In the dashboard go to Settings > View all settings > Payment receipts.
Select 'Spaces below Clover Mini receipt' to add more space at the bottom of the printed receipt.
Save.
entries.quote: Spaces below Clover Mini receipt: Select this option to add more spaces at the bottom of the Mini printed receipt to prevent information from being lost when tearing it off.

entries.title: Removing business details from receipts
steps: Some business information cannot be removed from receipts, for consumer protection.
The customer-facing business name, phone, email, address, website and logo can be changed in the account.
entries.quote: For consumer protection, some business information cannot be suppressed from receipts, but you can change your customer-facing business information.

entries.title: Find a past transaction on the device
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Enter the payment ID from the receipt in the search bar, or
scan the receipt barcode: on a Flex press and hold the scanner button on the left side; on other devices tap the barcode icon at the lower left, or
tap the filter icon at the top right.
Open the transaction to see the payment details.
entries.quote: To search by scanning, on a Clover Flex, press and hold the scanner button on the left side and scan.

entries.title: Find a past transaction on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Transactions.
Enter the payment ID in the search field, or choose a date range.
Select Search.
Narrow the results with the 'Filter by' options and select the transaction.
entries.quote: To search by ID, in the Search section, enter the payment ID in the search field.

entries.title: Customer says the charge does not show on their side
steps: Open the full transaction details on the dashboard.
Make sure the charge was completed and not voided.
Confirm the payment method, card type and last 4 digits.
Check whether the batch is closed.
If it is still unclear, contact support with the transaction ID.
entries.quote: Make sure the charge was completed and not voided.

entries.title: Show transactions for one employee
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Tap the filter icon at the top right.
From the dropdown, select Employees.
Select the employee name.
Tap Apply.
entries.quote: From the dropdown, select Employees.

entries.title: Show transactions from this device or another payment source
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Select the filter icon at the top right.
Tap All payment sources.
Choose Clover devices or Other payment sources.
For this device only: select All devices, choose This device, then Apply.
entries.quote: To filter by the device you're on, select All devices and choose This device to show only transactions made on the current device, then select Apply.

entries.title: Show transactions by payment type (cash, credit, debit...)
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Select the filter icon at the top right.
From the list, select Tenders.
Select a tender type.
Tap Apply.
entries.quote: From the drop-down list, select Tenders.

entries.title: Show only payments, refunds, auths or voids
steps: Open the Transactions app.
Select the filter icon at the top right.
From the list, select Transaction type.
Select Payment, Refund, Auth, Manual refund or Void.
Tap Apply.
entries.quote: From the drop-down list, select Transaction type.

entries.title: View or print the cash log on the device
steps: Open the Cash log app.
View the details: date, event, amount, reason and employee.
To print, tap the Printer icon at the top right. It is available on Clover Station, Flex and select Mini models.
entries.quote: View your cash log details, such as date, event, amount, reason, and employee.

entries.title: Run a cash log report on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Cash log.
Select a date range.
Filter by employees, events or device type, then search.
entries.quote: From the left, select Sales activity > Cash log.

entries.title: Run and print a report on the device (Reporting app)
steps: Open the Reporting app.
Select a report, such as Sale Overview, Employee Sales, Item Sales, Discounts or Taxes.
Select the date range.
Select Condensed report or Full report.
To print, tap the Printer icon at the top right.
entries.quote: Select the report type: Condensed report or Full report.

entries.title: No printer icon in the Cash log or Reporting app
steps: The printer icon is available on Clover Station, Flex and select Mini models only.
entries.quote: Note: The printer icon is available on Clover Station, Flex, and select Mini models.

entries.title: Run the Sales report on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Reports > Sales report.
Optionally pick a date range (up to one year at a time, within the past 5 years).
Optionally filter by employee, device, order type or section.
Select Print, or Options > Export.
entries.quote: From the left, select Reports > Sales report.

entries.title: A report shows no data
steps: Check the selected date range.
Check the filters applied, such as employee, device, order type or section.
Check whether any transactions happened in that period.
If data should be there and is not, contact support.
entries.quote: If no data appears for the selected timeframe, it may mean that no sales were recorded during that period.

entries.title: Report totals differ between employees or devices
steps: The employee who takes the order is credited with the sale.
The employee who processes the payment is credited with the amount collected.
The same applies to devices: one can create the order and another take the payment.
entries.quote: The employee who processes the payment is credited with the amount collected.

entries.title: Net sales, gross sales and amount collected on the Sales report
steps: Net sales: item sales after discounts and refunds; no tips, taxes, service charges or non-revenue sales.
Gross sales: sales before refunds; no tips, taxes or gift cards.
Amount collected: everything received, including tips, gift cards, taxes and non-revenue sales.
Unpaid balance: the value of partially paid orders.
entries.quote: Amount collected: Total amount received, including tips, gift cards, taxes, and non-revenue sales.

entries.title: Ask for a Sales report through the dashboard chat
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Help at the top right.
Select Start a chat.
Type the report request with details such as date range, employee or device.
Wait for the report, then select its link in the chat.
entries.quote: Enter your report request in the dialog box, including details such as date range, time of day, employee, device, or other filters.

entries.title: How far back reports go
steps: Up to 5 years of data are available on the dashboard.
Only one year can be selected at a time.
entries.quote: You can access up to 5 years of data in the dashboard, but you can select only one year at a time.

entries.title: Run the Employee sales report
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Reports > Employee sales.
Select a date range.
Optionally filter by device or order type.
Select Show results.
The user needs the Access Reporting > View employee report permission.
entries.quote: From the left, select Reports > Employee sales.

entries.title: Run the Order types report
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Reports > Order types.
Select a date range.
Optionally filter by employee, order type, provider or device.
Select Export for a CSV file, or Options to print.
entries.quote: From the left, select Reports > Order types.

entries.title: See all refunds (refunds report)
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Transactions.
Select the Refunds tab.
Optionally search by transaction ID, or filter by employee, amount or date range.
Optionally select 'Export refunds from this page' for a CSV file.
entries.quote: On the left, select Sales activity > Transactions.

entries.title: Turn on and run the Removed items report
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Reporting.
Under Customize reports, select edit and tick the Removed items report.
Then select Reports > Removed items, pick a date range and filters, and select Show results.
entries.quote: Under Customize reports, select edit and select the checkbox to turn on the Removed items report.

entries.title: Run the gift card report
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Reports > Gift cards.
Select the date range.
Optionally filter by load method (paid or complimentary).
Read, print or export the report.
entries.quote: From the left, select Reports > Gift cards.

entries.title: A gift card sale shows $0 gross sales
steps: This is expected. Selling a gift card counts as an amount collected, not a sale.
Example: a $100 gift card sold shows $0 gross sales and $100 collected.
When the card is redeemed, gross sales go up but amount collected does not.
entries.quote: Example: You sell a $100 gift card. Your Gross sale for that transaction is $0, whereas your amount collected is $100.

entries.title: Run the Sales overview full report
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Reports > Sales overview.
Select a date range.
Optionally use filters for employees, order types or devices.
Select Full report.
The total collected for all tenders should match the Amount collected on the sales summary.
entries.quote: Reconciliation: The total amount collected for all tenders should match the Amount collected on the sales summary.

entries.title: Trends report for more than three months does not open straight away
steps: A date range under three months opens the report automatically.
A range over three months submits a report request.
An email with a link arrives when it is ready; it is also under Reports > Requested Reports.
entries.quote: Select a date range of more than three (3) months to submit a report request.

entries.title: What 'Overpayment' and 'Repayments' mean on sales reports
steps: Overpayment: a payment amount above the order value, for example the same payment taken twice.
Repayment: a payment taken after a refund was processed; it shows in the Repayments line and in Gross sales.
entries.quote: An overpayment is a payment amount that exceeds the order value due to payment discrepancies or errors.

entries.title: Set business hours and time zone (used by reports and closeout)
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Business hours.
Under Hours of operation, select Edit, switch on the open days and set the times, then Save.
Under Timezone, select Edit, choose the time zone and Save.
Reports use the business time zone regardless of where you are.
entries.quote: When you run reports, the business time zone you selected is used regardless of your location.

entries.title: Create a discount on the device
steps: Open the Discounts app.
Tap the plus icon at the lower right.
Enter a name and either a percentage or an amount.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Tap the plus icon in the lower right corner.

entries.title: Create a discount on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Items > Discounts.
Select Add discount.
Enter a name and either a percentage or an amount.
Save.
entries.quote: From the left, select Items > Discounts.

entries.title: Add a tax rate or flat fee on the device
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Taxes & fees.
Tap Tax rates & fees.
Tap the add icon.
Enter a name.
Tap Tax percentage and enter the rate, or Flat fee and enter the amount.
Optionally tap Default to apply it to all items with default taxes turned on.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Enter a name in the Tax rate/fee field.

entries.title: Add a tax rate or flat fee on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Taxes and fees.
Select Set up taxes and fees, then Add tax rate or flat fee.
Enter a name and a percentage or fee amount.
Optionally tick Default.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Under Tax rates and fees, select Add tax rate or flat fee.

entries.title: No option to add taxes and fees
steps: Review the service plan on the dashboard; the option depends on the plan.
entries.quote: If you do not see an option to add taxes and fees, review your service plan on the dashboard.
entries.note: Changing the service plan is a billing matter.

entries.title: Exempt an order type from a tax or fee
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Taxes & fees.
Select 'Rules by order type', then 'Add exemption rule'.
Name the rule and select Next.
Choose the order type and the tax rates or fees to exempt.
Select Next, then Save.
entries.quote: Select 'Add exemption rule'.

entries.title: Taxes and flat fees must not be used as a card surcharge
steps: Do not use the taxes and flat fees option to recover card processing costs.
It is a violation of card brand rules and may result in fines.
entries.quote: Using the taxes and flat fees option to recover card payment processing costs is a violation of card brand rules and regulations, which may result in fines.

entries.title: Add a service charge (for example auto gratuity) on the device
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Additional charges.
Tick 'Enable service charge'.
Select Add service charge and enter the name and percentage.
Optionally tick 'Auto gratuity' (one active at a time) or 'Taxable fees'.
Select Save.
Up to eight service charges can be created.
entries.quote: Tap Additional charges.

entries.title: A service charge must not be used to cover card fees
steps: Service charges cannot be used to recover credit card processing costs.
Doing so may result in fines or penalties from the card networks.
Card costs are recovered only through the Clover Credit Surcharge program.
entries.quote: Important: Service charges cannot be used to recover credit card processing costs.

entries.title: Turning on credit card surcharging
steps: Surcharging is added to the service plan by support; it cannot be switched on by the merchant.
It applies to credit cards only, not debit or prepaid cards.
It is prohibited in some U.S. states.
entries.quote: To add surcharging to your service plan, contact Clover support.

entries.title: No surcharge on a Clover Go payment (Limited Mode)
steps: Surcharges are not applied to payments taken in Limited Mode on Clover Go.
Clover Go enters Limited Mode automatically during system maintenance and shows a message when full function is back.
Surcharges are also not applied on the Clover Go G1 app or with audio jack readers.
entries.quote: Note: Your Clover Go device automatically enters Limited Mode during that time and displays a message when full functionality is restored.

entries.title: Set or change an employee's passcode on the device
steps: Open the Employees app.
Select the employee.
Select the edit icon at the top right.
Select the Passcode field and enter a new passcode.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Select the Passcode field and input a new passcode.

entries.title: Set or change an employee's passcode on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Employees.
Select Edit (pencil icon) next to the employee.
Under Passcode, enter a passcode.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select Edit (pencil icon) next to the employee you want to create a passcode for.

entries.title: Switch between 4-digit and 6-digit passcodes
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Employees.
Select Options > Device passcode.
Select Change in the Passcode length section.
Enter new passcodes for each employee, or select Autofill passcodes.
Select Save.
Autofill removes the last two digits when going to 4 digits, and adds 00 when going to 6 digits.
entries.quote: If you switch from 4-digit to 6-digit passcodes, choosing Autofill passcodes adds “00” to the end of each passcode.

entries.title: Passcode length rules
steps: Passcodes are 4 or 6 digits, and all passcodes on a device must be the same length.
Merchants onboarded before April 2026 can switch between the two at any time.
From April 2026, new merchants must use 6-digit passcodes.
entries.quote: Note: Effective April 2026, new merchants must use 6-digit passcodes.

entries.title: A new passcode is not accepted
steps: Use a 6-digit passcode.
It must not be repeating numbers such as 111111.
It must not be sequential numbers such as 123456.
entries.quote: You must use a 6-digit passcode that does not contain repeating (e.g., 111111) or sequential (e.g., 123456) numbers.

entries.title: Change an employee's phone number or passcode
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard as an admin or owner.
Select Employees.
Select the employee from the list.
Select Edit and update the phone number or passcode.
Select Save.
The employee uses the new passcode the next time they log in on the device.
entries.quote: Yes. The employee must use the new passcode the next time they log in on their Clover device.

entries.title: Change an employee's name or email address
steps: The name and email cannot be edited.
Delete the employee profile and create a new one.
If the same email address is reused, wait 24 hours before adding the new employee.
entries.quote: To change an employee's full name or email address, you must delete the profile and create a new employee.

entries.title: 'We are unable to verify the phone number entered. Please enter a valid mobile number'
steps: Two-factor authentication may already be enabled on the account. With it on, the phone number cannot be changed from the dashboard.
Contact support and ask for two-factor authentication to be disabled.
Then update the phone number in the dashboard.
Turn two-factor authentication back on with the new number.
Make sure the number is a mobile number (not landline or VoIP), has the right area code, and can receive texts; enter it without spaces or symbols.
entries.quote: If you see the message 'We are unable to verify the phone number entered. Please enter a valid mobile number,' two-factor authentication (2FA) may already be enabled on your account.

entries.title: Update your own profile on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Profile, select Edit.
Change your information and select Save.
entries.quote: Under Profile, select Edit to change your personal information.

entries.title: Change an employee's role on the device
steps: Open the Employees app.
Select the employee.
Select Edit at the top right.
Choose a role from the Role dropdown.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select an employee role from the Role dropdown list.

entries.title: Change what a role is allowed to do, on the device
steps: Open the Employees app.
Select the Permissions tab.
Tick or clear the checkboxes for each role.
entries.quote: Select or clear the checkboxes to enable or remove permissions for each employee role.

entries.title: Change what a role is allowed to do, on the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings, then Employee permissions under Employees.
Select Edit next to a feature.
Tick or clear the checkbox next to each role.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select Edit next to a feature to modify its permissions.

entries.title: Create a new employee role
steps: Open the Employees app.
Select Roles.
Select the add button at the bottom right.
Enter the role name.
Select a default role to base it on: Admin, Manager or Employee.
Select Add Role.
entries.quote: Select the add button in the bottom right.

entries.title: Default roles cannot be removed
steps: There are three default roles: Admin, Manager and Employee.
They cannot be removed; custom roles can be added and deleted.
entries.quote: You cannot remove default employee roles like Admin, Employee, and Manager.

entries.title: Add an employee
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard, or open the Clover Go app.
On the dashboard select Employees > Employees list; on Clover Go select More > Employees > Manage.
Select Add employee.
Enter the details. An email address is needed for dashboard access.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Note: An email address is required to give employees access to the dashboard.

entries.title: Cannot add more than three employees
steps: The Starter plan supports up to three employees, including the owner or admin.
All other plans allow unlimited employee profiles.
entries.quote: The Starter plan supports up to three employees, including the owner or admin, while all other plans offer unlimited employee profiles.
entries.note: Changing plan is a billing matter.

entries.title: Set up two-factor authentication by text message
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Profile, select Edit your profile.
Select Two-factor authentication, then Turn on two-factor authentication.
Select SMS, then Next.
Enter the mobile number and select Send code.
Enter the code and select Next.
entries.quote: Select Two-factor authentication, then Turn on two-factor authentication.

entries.title: Set up two-factor authentication with an authenticator app
steps: Install an authenticator app on the phone, for example Google Authenticator.
Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings, then Edit your profile under Profile.
Select Two-factor authentication and turn it on.
Select Authenticator app, then Next. A QR code appears.
Scan the QR code with the phone and add the token.
Enter the verification code and select Next.
entries.quote: Select Authenticator app and then select Next. A QR code appears.

entries.title: Download backup recovery codes for two-factor authentication
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Profile, select Edit your profile.
Scroll to Recovery codes and select 'Download a new set of recovery codes'.
Keep the file in a safe place. The codes let you log in when the phone is not available.
entries.quote: If you don't have your phone available, you can use the recovery codes to log in to your Clover account.

entries.title: What needs two-factor authentication
steps: Clover requires all merchants to set up two-factor authentication.
It must be on to issue refunds; the Refund button does not appear without it.
It must be on for an owner to change bank account information.
entries.quote: Note: Two-factor authentication must be turned on to issue refunds in the Transactions app; the Refund button doesn't appear unless two-factor authentication is turned on.

entries.title: Clover Go shows 'Are you trying to access?'
steps: This appears when Clover Go is enabled for step-up authentication and an action on the dashboard needs extra verification.
Select 'Yes, it's me' to approve, or 'No, don't allow'.
entries.quote: you’ll receive a message in the Clover Go app that says, 'Are you trying to access?'

entries.title: Use the Clover Go app to approve verification requests
steps: Open the Clover Go app.
Select More > Settings.
Select Your profile.
On the 'Authenticate easily with Clover Go' screen, select Enable.
Enter the 6-digit code sent to the phone and tap Submit.
SMS or an authenticator app is still used to sign in to the dashboard.
entries.quote: On the Authenticate easily with Clover Go screen, select Enable.

entries.title: Change the owner's login email address
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
From the Profile menu at the top right, select your name.
Select Edit next to Email address.
Enter the 6-digit code sent to the current email and select Submit.
Enter the new email and select Continue, then Confirm.
Enter the 6-digit code sent to the new email and select Submit.
You are logged out; use the reset link sent to the new email to set a password.
If there is no Edit option, contact support.
entries.quote: Note: If you do not see the Edit option, contact Clover support to change your email address.

entries.title: Change the mobile number used for two-factor authentication
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
From the Profile menu at the top right, select your name.
Select Edit next to Mobile number.
Update the number and select Save.
entries.quote: This is the phone number used for two-factor authentication. Anyone with a Clover account can edit their mobile number.
entries.note: The Edit employee profiles article says the number cannot be changed while 2FA is enabled; see the 'unable to verify the phone number' entry.

entries.title: Changing the bank account for deposits
steps: Only the account owner can do this, with two-factor authentication enabled.
In the dashboard: Settings > View all settings > Bank information > Change bank account.
The current account number on file must be entered first, then the new details are verified through the bank or with a voided check.
If it cannot be completed in the dashboard, support will ask for a voided check, bank statement or bank letter; updates typically take 48 to 72 hours.
entries.quote: Only account owners can manage bank account information.

entries.title: 'Try again in 24 hours' when updating the bank account
steps: This can appear when the bank account was recently opened or updated and its information is not yet available.
New or recently updated accounts may take 2 to 7 days to appear.
Wait up to 7 days and try again.
If it still fails after 7 days, contact support.
entries.quote: If your bank account was recently opened or updated, you may receive a Try again in 24 hours message while account information becomes available.

entries.title: Bank account update is locked after wrong account numbers
steps: Entering an incorrect bank account number three times locks the update process.
Contact support (the article says Clover support).
entries.quote: Warning: If you enter an incorrect bank account number three times, access to the update process is locked. You must contact Clover support for assistance.

entries.title: Deposit is late, lower than expected, or missing
steps: The standard funding schedule is 1-3 business days.
Reasons listed: account verification on a new account, ACH rejects (wrong or closed bank details), risk review, fraud investigation, backup withholding for tax information, or a collection balance.
Most delays need information or action from the merchant; once provided, funds are usually released within 24 to 48 hours.
entries.quote: Once you provide the necessary information and complete the required steps, most funding issues will be resolved, and funds will be released within 24 to 48 hours.

entries.title: Deposit rejected by the bank (ACH reject)
steps: Causes listed: incorrect bank details, a closed account, an account under review, or the bank blocking the account.
Verify the account is funded and the bank details are correct.
Failed transfers are not retried automatically.
If the details are correct, contact support.
entries.quote: Note: Failed transactions are not retried. You need to reinitiate the transaction after the issue is resolved.

entries.title: Deposit is different from the batch total
steps: It may be due to daily billing fees, deductions for rejected transactions, or chargebacks.
With daily billing, the discount rate and per-transaction fees are collected when the batch closes.
Rejected transactions and chargebacks are deducted when the batch closes.
entries.quote: If your deposit amount differs from the batch total, it may be due to daily billing fees, deductions from rejected transactions, or chargebacks.

entries.title: View monthly statements
steps: Only the account owner can view billing statements.
Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Billing & statements, select Monthly statements.
Select the statement; download or print the PDF if needed.
entries.quote: Under Billing & statements, select Monthly statements. To see statements for previous years, click the arrow.

entries.title: Why some transactions have higher fees
steps: Card-not-present payments usually have higher fees.
To avoid higher fees, insert or swipe the card whenever possible.
Voiding a payment typically has no fees, unlike a refund.
entries.quote: To avoid higher fees, insert or swipe payment cards whenever possible.

entries.title: Sales activity totals do not match the statement or deposits
steps: This is normal: Sales activity shows real-time gross sales by transaction date; the statement shows funded amounts after fees.
Differences come from settlement timing, refunds and voids, late tips, offline transactions, fees, chargebacks and third-party payouts.
To reconcile: compare settlement dates, review refunds and voids separately, check for offline transactions or delayed batches, and match net deposits rather than gross sales.
For unexplained differences, contact support with the MID, date range, deposit amounts and screenshots.
entries.quote: Compare settlement dates, not transaction dates.

entries.title: Questions about fees on the Merchant Processing Statement
steps: The statement can include start-up, account and conditional fees; types and amounts vary by account.
Fee questions go to support, not Scout.
entries.quote: Fee types and amounts vary based on your account, services, and processing activity.

entries.title: Questions about processing fees (interchange, batch, chargeback fees)
steps: The Merchant Processing Statement lists transaction, chargeback, monthly and conditional fees.
Fee questions go to support, not Scout.
entries.quote: The Merchant Processing Statement provides detailed information about fees for payment processing activities.

entries.title: Questions about plan, app and cellular fees
steps: The Clover Plan & App Statement lists service plan, app subscription and cellular data fees.
Fee questions go to support, not Scout.
entries.quote: Cellular data fee: Monthly fee for cellular data.

entries.title: Changing the Clover service plan
steps: Plan changes affect billing and which features are available; review any contractual obligations first.
Route plan and pricing questions to client services.
entries.quote: Ensure you review any contractual obligations before changing plans.

entries.title: Complete the yearly PCI self-assessment questionnaire
steps: Open Clover Security Plus from a task or notification on the dashboard, or from a link in a Clover Security Plus email.
Log in and answer the questions about how customer data is protected.
Depending on the answers, there may be more questions and a quarterly network scan.
Not verifying compliance can add a monthly fee shown as 'non-receipt of PCI validation'.
entries.quote: These may appear as “non-receipt of PCI validation” on your processing fee statements.

entries.title: Check PCI compliance status
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under About your business, select PCI compliance.
Review the expiration date and status. A banner shows if the status is Non-compliant.
Select Go to Clover Security to complete the required steps.
entries.quote: Under About your business, select PCI compliance.

entries.title: Maximum sale exceeded
steps: A fraud rule on the account blocks any single transaction greater than a set amount.
To change it, log in to the dashboard and go to Settings > View all settings > Fraud Tools (under Ecommerce).
In Transaction Amount and Velocity Limits, select Edit and adjust the rule.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Message: Maximum sale exceeded

entries.title: Below minimum sale
steps: A fraud rule on the account blocks any single transaction less than a set amount.
To change it, log in to the dashboard and go to Settings > View all settings > Fraud Tools (under Ecommerce).
In Transaction Amount and Velocity Limits, select Edit and adjust the rule.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Message: Below minimum sale

entries.title: Merchant volume exceeded
steps: A fraud rule on the account limits either the transaction total or the number of transactions the business can accept, and the limit was reached.
To change it, log in to the dashboard and go to Settings > View all settings > Fraud Tools (under Ecommerce).
In Transaction Amount and Velocity Limits, select Edit and adjust the rule.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Message: Merchant volume exceeded

entries.title: Card volume exceeded
steps: A fraud rule on the account limits the number of transactions per card, and this card reached it.
To change it, log in to the dashboard and go to Settings > View all settings > Fraud Tools (under Ecommerce).
In Transaction Amount and Velocity Limits, select Edit and adjust the rule.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Message: Card volume exceeded

entries.title: Online or keyed payment voided for an address or postal code mismatch (AVS)
steps: The Address Verification System checks the postal code and street address against the card issuer's records.
Clover includes a rule that blocks payments failing postal code verification.
Rules are under Settings > View all settings > Fraud Tools > Address Verification System (AVS) > Edit.
entries.quote: Clover includes a rule to block any payments that fail postal code verification.

entries.title: Online or keyed payment voided for a CVV mismatch
steps: If the CVV rule is on, a CVV that does not match the one on file at the customer's bank makes the system void the transaction.
